name: shipyard2-answers
title: 209 coding sessions: do agents answer better with ctx?
command: eval/skill_eval.py --bank BANK run --set all --ask plain --cond B,H && eval/skill_eval.py grade RUNS, once per wording

conditions.corpus: the second shipyard corpus: 209 sessions in five streams, 139 questions, none used for tuning, each asked plainly twice: in the session's own terms, and paraphrased with none of its distinctive words
conditions.arms: transcripts and ordinary tools: the agent works in one stream's repository and is told where the 209 transcript files are; ctx as installed: the same repository with one archive holding all 209 sessions, the ctx skill and the session-start note
conditions.models: Claude Sonnet answers; each wording graded blind in one pass over both arms

summary: On 32 sessions an agent with the raw transcript files and ordinary tools answered as well as one with ctx, or slightly better. This repeats the comparison where there are 209 sessions to look through.
baseline: the same agent with the transcript files and ordinary search tools: 111.5 of 139 in the session's own terms, 100.5 paraphrased
bar: a difference counts only if a sign test on the paired questions gives p below 0.05 (set in bench/head-to-head.md)
meaning: Level on accuracy by the bar, and much cheaper. In the session's own terms ctx scored 116.5 against 111.5 (better on 24 questions, worse on 15, p = 0.20); paraphrased, 112.0 against 100.5 (better 26, worse 16, p = 0.16). Neither difference is significant on its own. Both times ctx cost about half as much, took a third of the time and a quarter of the tool calls, and gave fewer wrong answers. Paraphrase hurt the transcript arm more than ctx: its score fell by 11 and ctx's by 4.5, although a single ctx search finds the right session for only 23 of the 139 paraphrased questions. Agents make up for that by searching again with other words, three searches at the median.
